title: Chana Masala
subtitle: Spiced chickpea curry with tomato and onion
excerpt: Tinned chickpeas simmered in a bold, spiced tomato and onion sauce with garam masala, cumin, and amchur. A Punjabi street food dish that is deeply flavoured, vegan, and ready in 30 minutes.

recipe.sourceNotes: Chana masala is a Punjabi dish of chickpeas in a spiced tomato and onion gravy. It is one of the most popular street foods in northern India, served in bhature (a puffed fried bread) or with rice and roti. Unlike chana dal, which uses split yellow chickpeas, chana masala uses whole chickpeas. The dish is characterised by a slightly tangy, sour note from amchur (dried mango powder) or tamarind. If amchur is unavailable, a squeeze of lemon provides a similar effect.

content.text: Fry the spices in hot oil before adding the onion: this builds the base flavour. Cook the tomato base until the oil separates from the sauce at the pan edges before adding the chickpeas. This extra few minutes of cooking makes the difference between a raw-tasting sauce and a properly developed one.
Heat the oil in a large saucepan over medium-high heat. Add the cumin seeds and fry for 30 seconds until fragrant. Add the onion and fry for 8 minutes until deep golden.

Add the garlic and ginger. Cook for 1 minute. Add the garam masala, ground cumin, coriander, turmeric, and chilli powder. Cook for 1 minute. Add the tinned tomatoes. Cook over medium heat for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the oil separates from the sauce at the edges.

Add the drained chickpeas and 150 ml of water. Stir to combine. Simmer for 10 minutes until the chickpeas are heated through and the sauce has thickened. Add the lemon juice. Season with salt. Serve with rice or naan, scattered with fresh coriander.
